author: Janson McNair
title: 'You matter.' Mental health walker's 12,000-mile trek hits Taunton - NewsBreak
text:
By Janson McNair ,
1 days ago Kyndal Ray Edwards is getting his steps in.
The 33-year-old from Orange Park, Florida, has spent the past five years working to complete a walk across the nation. His reason? Advocating for mental health .
"In 2013, I was doing a year in the county jail in Florida when I read a newspaper article about a gentleman who had walked from Tallahassee, Florida to Laguna Beach, California, (and I) fell in love with the story," he said. "(I) got out in 2014 (and) tried to put together a walk to take off on January 1, 2015 ... (But) ended up going (back) to prison instead."
Edwards said he's spent a lot of time in and out of prison for various burglary charges, but his walking mission is one of the things that has grounded his recovery.
"I was more addicted to crime than I was to ... drugs itself," he said. "In early April 2019, during (a) five-year prison sentence, I made a decision to change my life."
"My last year, I was in a work release program. I remembered that I wanted to walk across America, and I was like 'If I did walk across America, what would I walk for?" he said. "And every single day on social media, somebody was posting about another loss of life to a drug overdose or suicide ... So I decided to pick mental health and recovery."
Edwards less than 400 miles from his finish line Edwards' walking journey includes "all four corners of the lower 48 states of America," in the name of mental health and recovery and in remembrance of those who have lost their lives to overdoses or suicide.
With a few hundred miles left in his journey, Edwards made it to Massachusetts last week, passing through Taunton, Raynham, Middleboro, Plymouth, Rockland and Kingston. He said his final destination is the West Quoddy Head Lighthouse in Lubec, Maine, the northeastern point of the lower 48 states.
"As of now, I am over 89 months drug free over seven years (and) five months since I've changed my life," Edwards said, "and almost 12,000 miles (in)."
Edwards said last week he had approximately 375 miles left to walk.
"I'm right at 11,773 miles complete," he said. "I have crossed 37 state lines (and) 30 different states ... There's a couple different states that I crossed twice, just totally different sections at different times on the journey."

'There's too many people that feel hopeless and lonely and feel like people don't care' Edwards said he arrived in Massachusetts as the Northeast was dealing with impacts from the nor'easter that rolled in over the weekend.
"I was definitely out in the rain," he said. "There were periods where it did rain a little bit harder for a bit at a time, but honestly, even though it was consistent, the rain was pretty light."
Edwards said he is making the most of his time in the state, making sure to see some of the popular sites like Fenway Park and Boston Common.
"Since actually showing up at the Massachusetts state line, it's been pretty incredible," he said. "People met me at the line, (and) somebody gave me a Dunkin' hat ... (People are) pretty awesome up here."
Edwards said when it's all said and done, he hopes his journey inspires people to keep going, no matter what they're going through.
"There's too many people that feel hopeless and lonely and feel like people don't care," he said. "I want people to know that they're cared about, that there's somebody out here that maybe they don't (know) in person but they care and that they're loved."
Edwards said his message in his advocacy comes down to two simple words.
"You matter," he said.
This article originally appeared on The Enterprise: 'You matter.' Mental health walker's 12,000-mile trek hits Taunton
